sections.title: Starting up and ideas
sections.covers: Deciding to start, finding an idea worth working on, and the first weeks of a company.

sections.title: Finding product-market fit
sections.covers: Talking to users, shipping a minimum product, and measuring whether the market pulls.

sections.title: Fundraising
sections.covers: Raising seed and priced rounds: instruments, term sheets, pitching, and runway math.

sections.title: Hiring and culture
sections.covers: Recruiting, interviewing, compensation, and the management systems that scale a team.

sections.title: Growth and distribution
sections.covers: First users, growth loops, channel decay, and when to scale spend and headcount.

sections.title: Pricing and sales
sections.covers: Setting and raising prices, founder-led selling, and building the first sales team.

sections.title: Exits and acquisitions
sections.covers: Deciding whether to sell, running an acquisition process, and life after the deal.

entries.title: How to Start a Startup
entries.author: Paul Graham
entries.teaches: A startup needs good people, something customers actually want, and low spending; most failures trace to missing one of the three.

entries.title: How to Get Startup Ideas
entries.author: Paul Graham
entries.teaches: Notice problems you have yourself instead of thinking up ideas; well-shaped ideas look like a deep well of demand, not a shallow puddle of mild interest.

entries.title: Startups in 13 Sentences
entries.author: Paul Graham
entries.teaches: Thirteen compressed rules for the early company, from picking cofounders through launching fast, understanding users, and refusing to be demoralized.

entries.title: Before the Startup
entries.author: Paul Graham
entries.teaches: Startups are counterintuitive: trusting expertise over instinct, needing users more than tricks, and why gaming the system stops working.

entries.title: Startup Playbook
entries.author: Sam Altman
entries.teaches: An end-to-end primer on idea, product, team, execution, and fundraising, written as the condensed version of YC's partner advice.

entries.title: How To Be Successful
entries.author: Sam Altman
entries.teaches: Compound yourself, have almost too much self-belief, and focus: work out what matters most and say no to nearly everything else.

entries.title: How to Start a Startup, Lecture 1
entries.author: Sam Altman and Dustin Moskovitz
entries.teaches: The opening lecture of the Stanford CS183B course: why to start a startup (and why not), and the idea-product-team-execution frame the rest of the course follows.

entries.title: Zero to One
entries.author: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters
entries.teaches: Build something new rather than copying what works: escape competition toward monopoly, hold a definite view of the future, and nail distribution deliberately.

entries.title: Founders at Work
entries.author: Jessica Livingston
entries.teaches: Interviews with the founders of Apple, PayPal, Hotmail, and dozens more about what the earliest days actually looked like, pivots and rejections included.

entries.title: I'm Launching 12 Startups in 12 Months
entries.author: Pieter Levels
entries.teaches: Ship many small products on a public deadline and let the market pick the winner, instead of betting years on one unvalidated idea.

entries.title: The Only Thing That Matters
entries.author: Marc Andreessen
entries.teaches: The essay that named product-market fit: market beats team and product, you can always feel when fit is absent, and the only goal before fit is to get there.

entries.title: How Superhuman Built an Engine to Find Product/Market Fit
entries.author: Rahul Vohra
entries.teaches: Turn the very-disappointed survey question into an operating metric: segment the users who would miss you most and build the roadmap from their feedback.

entries.title: The Mom Test
entries.author: Rob Fitzpatrick
entries.teaches: How to run customer conversations that produce facts: ask about the customer's life and past behavior, never pitch, and never ask whether they would buy.

entries.title: The Lean Startup: Methodology Principles
entries.author: Eric Ries
entries.teaches: The build-measure-learn loop, validated learning, and innovation accounting: treat every product decision as a testable hypothesis.

entries.title: Why the Lean Start-Up Changes Everything
entries.author: Steve Blank
entries.teaches: The customer-development case in one article: a startup is a search for a business model, so test hypotheses with customers instead of executing a five-year plan.

entries.title: How to Talk to Users
entries.author: Eric Migicovsky
entries.teaches: A YC Startup School session on user interviews: extract the problem, its cost, and current workarounds without contaminating the answers with your pitch.

entries.title: How to Plan an MVP
entries.author: Michael Seibel
entries.teaches: Scope a lean MVP you can build in weeks: hold the problem tightly and the solution loosely, launch to a small set of users, and iterate.

entries.title: 12 Things about Product-Market Fit
entries.author: Tren Griffin
entries.teaches: A synthesis of how Andreessen, Rachleff, and others define and detect fit, including why growth tactics cannot compensate for its absence.

entries.title: How to Raise Money
entries.author: Paul Graham
entries.teaches: Treat fundraising as a discrete phase run in parallel with nothing: get the first commitment, create urgency, close fast, and get back to building.

entries.title: How to Convince Investors
entries.author: Paul Graham
entries.teaches: Convince yourself first: investors fund formidable founders making true claims about a big market, not polished pitches.

entries.title: The Equity Equation
entries.author: Paul Graham
entries.teaches: Give up n% of the company only when it makes the remaining (1 - n) worth more than the whole was before; one formula for investors, hires, and advisors alike.

entries.title: Default Alive or Default Dead?
entries.author: Paul Graham
entries.teaches: Know whether current growth reaches profitability on remaining cash before entertaining any expansive plan; fundraising is not a substitute for the answer.

entries.title: A Guide to Seed Fundraising
entries.author: Geoff Ralston
entries.teaches: The mechanics of a seed round end to end: how much to raise, SAFEs versus priced equity, valuation, investor meetings, and closing documents.

entries.title: Safe Financing Documents
entries.author: Y Combinator
entries.teaches: The canonical post-money SAFE templates and user guide, the instrument most US seed rounds are actually papered on.

entries.title: Venture Deals
entries.author: Brad Feld and Jason Mendelson
entries.teaches: Term sheets clause by clause: economics versus control, how VC funds work internally, and how negotiation leverage actually shifts during a round.

entries.title: Term Sheet Series
entries.author: Brad Feld
entries.teaches: The blog series that became Venture Deals: one post per term sheet clause, explaining which terms carry economics, which carry control, and which are noise.

entries.title: Invest in Lines, Not Dots
entries.author: Mark Suster
entries.teaches: Investors fund trajectories, not snapshots: build relationships early so each meeting plots another point on the line of your execution.

entries.title: How to Pitch Your Startup
entries.author: Kevin Hale
entries.teaches: A YC Startup School session on pitch construction: lead with what you do in plain words, make the market obvious, and optimize for being understood.

entries.title: Writing a Business Plan
entries.author: Sequoia Capital
entries.teaches: The pitch outline Sequoia asks founders to follow: problem, solution, why now, market size, competition, product, business model, team, and financials.

entries.title: How to Hire
entries.author: Sam Altman
entries.teaches: Spend a third of your time recruiting, hire slowly, value aptitude over experience, and treat every early hire as culture-defining.

entries.title: Netflix Culture
entries.author: Netflix
entries.teaches: The maintained statement of the management philosophy Netflix's 2009 culture deck introduced: a dream team of high performers, candor, and context over control.

entries.title: How Netflix Reinvented HR
entries.author: Patty McCord
entries.teaches: The thinking behind the culture deck from its co-author: hire fully formed adults, tell the truth about performance, and drop policies that manage the bottom 3%.

entries.title: The Guerrilla Guide to Interviewing (version 3.0)
entries.author: Joel Spolsky
entries.teaches: Hire people who are smart and get things done: a concrete technical-interview protocol, and why a maybe is always a no.

entries.title: Good Product Manager / Bad Product Manager
entries.author: Ben Horowitz
entries.teaches: Role definition by contrast, written to train Netscape PMs: the good/bad format that became the standard way to write any job's expectations.

entries.title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
entries.author: Ben Horowitz
entries.teaches: Managing through the struggle: layoffs, demoting friends, wartime versus peacetime CEOs, and why most management advice skips the hard parts.

entries.title: High Growth Handbook
entries.author: Elad Gil
entries.teaches: Scaling from 10 to 1,000 people: executive hiring, board management, reorganizations, late-stage fundraising, and M&A, with operator interviews.

entries.title: High Output Management
entries.author: Andrew S. Grove
entries.teaches: Management as manufacturing: managerial leverage, one-on-ones, meetings as a medium of work, and the objective-setting system that OKRs descend from.

entries.title: How to Operate
entries.author: Keith Rabois
entries.teaches: A CS183B lecture on running a company: management as maximizing output, editing instead of writing, metrics pairing, and spotting barrels versus ammunition.

entries.title: Give Away Your Legos and Other Commandments for Scaling Startups
entries.author: Molly Graham
entries.teaches: Scaling a team means handing your job to new people and finding a new one, and the anxiety that provokes is a sign the company is growing correctly.

entries.title: The Holloway Guide to Equity Compensation
entries.author: Holloway
entries.teaches: Options, RSUs, vesting, 409A valuations, and the tax consequences of each, written for the employees and founders who have to make the decisions.

entries.title: Startup = Growth
entries.author: Paul Graham
entries.teaches: A startup is a company designed to grow fast; pick a weekly growth rate and let hitting it decide nearly everything else.

entries.title: Do Things that Don't Scale
entries.author: Paul Graham
entries.teaches: Recruit the first users one at a time and give them unscalably good treatment; the Airbnb door-to-door and Stripe install-it-for-you examples come from here.

entries.title: Growth (How to Start a Startup, Lecture 6)
entries.author: Alex Schultz
entries.teaches: Facebook's growth lead on retention as the foundation of growth, picking a north-star metric, and the magic-moment framing of activation.

entries.title: How to Get Users and Grow
entries.author: Gustaf Alströmer
entries.teaches: A YC Startup School session mapping the acquisition channels that actually work for early startups and why growth tactics fail before product-market fit.

entries.title: The Law of Shitty Clickthroughs
entries.author: Andrew Chen
entries.teaches: Every marketing channel decays as it saturates, so durable growth comes from finding channels early and building loops competitors cannot copy.

entries.title: Why Product Market Fit Isn't Enough
entries.author: Brian Balfour
entries.teaches: Opens the four-fits series: product-market, product-channel, channel-model, and model-market fit have to line up together for a growth engine to work.

entries.title: 1,000 True Fans
entries.author: Kevin Kelly
entries.teaches: A creator or niche product can sustain itself on a thousand people who will buy anything you make, reached directly rather than through mass channels.

entries.title: Blitzscaling (Harvard Business Review interview)
entries.author: Reid Hoffman
entries.teaches: The case for prioritizing speed over efficiency under uncertainty: in winner-take-most markets, being first to scale beats being right about costs.

entries.title: Blitzscaling
entries.author: Reid Hoffman and Chris Yeh
entries.teaches: The full playbook behind the interview: which fires to let burn at each company stage, and how business-model innovation drives scale more than product.

entries.title: How the Biggest Consumer Apps Got Their First 1,000 Users
entries.author: Lenny Rachitsky
entries.teaches: Case evidence across major consumer apps that early acquisition was manual and unscalable: going where users already were, one channel at a time.

entries.title: Why Your Customers Would Be Happier If You Charged More
entries.author: Patrick McKenzie with Ramit Sethi
entries.teaches: Underpricing hurts customers as well as revenue: price on value delivered, segment with tiers, and raise prices more often than feels comfortable.

entries.title: Pricing Low-Touch SaaS
entries.author: Patrick McKenzie
entries.teaches: A Stripe Atlas guide to self-serve SaaS pricing: value metrics, tier design, annual plans, and running price changes without burning existing customers.

entries.title: Startup Pricing 101
entries.author: Kevin Hale
entries.teaches: A YC Startup School session on cost-, competitor-, and value-based pricing, why startups should usually raise prices, and the 10-5-20 rule of thumb.

entries.title: How to Sell
entries.author: Tyler Bosmeny
entries.teaches: Founder-led sales from the Clever CEO: founders are the first salespeople, the funnel is prospecting-to-close, and talking to users doubles as pipeline.

entries.title: The Price Is Right: Essential Tips for Nailing Your Pricing Strategy
entries.author: First Round Review
entries.teaches: Pricing as positioning: anchoring, decoy tiers, and why the price you choose tells the market what category you are in.

entries.title: Five Ways to Build a $100 Million Business
entries.author: Christoph Janz
entries.teaches: The elephants-deer-rabbits-mice-flies frame: your average revenue per account determines how many customers you need and therefore which sales motion is viable.

entries.title: The 48 Types of VP Sales. Make Deadly Sure You Hire the Right One
entries.author: Jason Lemkin
entries.teaches: VP Sales candidates vary on deal size, sales motion, and stage fit; hiring one mismatched on any axis fails even when the person is genuinely good.

entries.title: Predictable Revenue
entries.author: Aaron Ross and Marylou Tyler
entries.teaches: The outbound playbook built at Salesforce: separate prospecting from closing, run cold outreach as a measurable process, and staff specialized sales roles.

entries.title: The Sales Acceleration Formula
entries.author: Mark Roberge
entries.teaches: Scaling sales as an engineering problem, from HubSpot's first sales hire to $100M: the same hiring rubric, training, and comp plan applied to every rep.

entries.title: Notes on the Acquisition Process
entries.author: Chris Dixon
entries.teaches: Startups are bought, not sold: build relationships with acquirers early, create real alternatives, and run the process without deceptive pressure tactics.

entries.title: Should You Sell Your Company?
entries.author: Ben Horowitz
entries.teaches: The two-question test for any offer: is the market an order of magnitude bigger than exploited so far, and will you be number one in it; two yeses mean keep building.

entries.title: 5 Reasons to Sell Your Startup
entries.author: Elad Gil
entries.teaches: The legitimate reasons to take an offer, from an above-trajectory price to founder burnout and market windows closing, and how to tell them from distraction.

entries.title: M&A Ladder: Position Your Startup to Sell It for More
entries.author: Elad Gil
entries.teaches: Acquirers price teams, products, strategic assets, and businesses on different multiples; moving up that ladder changes what the same company is worth.

entries.title: Finish Big
entries.author: Bo Burlingham
entries.teaches: Interviews with owners who sold: the eight factors that separate founders who are glad they exited from those who regret it, starting years before the deal.

entries.title: When Should You Sell Your Company?
entries.author: Jason Lemkin
entries.teaches: Sell when you have a great offer and are out of energy to go big, and otherwise keep compounding; lukewarm sales processes produce the worst outcomes.

entries.title: Rich vs. King in the Real World: Why I Sold My Company
entries.author: Jason Cohen
entries.teaches: A first-person application of the rich-versus-king tradeoff: what selling Smart Bear changed, and how to decide which outcome you actually want.

entries.title: The Founder's Dilemma
entries.author: Noam Wasserman
entries.teaches: The research behind rich versus king: choices that maximize wealth and choices that maximize control diverge early, and few founders get both.
